themes.name: Preview/unstable style features and stabilization (string_processing, hug_parens, dict values)
Line splitting and style choices for long expressions
Configuration, file discovery and gitignore handling

top_issues.reason: Security hardening: a project-relative cache-dir lets attacker-controlled pickle files run arbitrary code when Black runs with caching on.
Silent correctness bug: files that git tracks are skipped when a nested .gitignore re-includes them, and --check still passes. A concrete fix has been proposed.
Tracking issue for deciding the 2027 stable style; it affects every user and many preview-style issues depend on it.
Target-version inference from requires-python (~=3.11.0) picks Python versions the project doesn't support. PRs are already open, and it is related to #3581.
Black hangs forever on deeply nested dicts, a performance bug that can block CI.

records.judge_reason: The report's themes closely match the labelled ones. The string processing/preview theme is the same, plus #5658 (2027 stable style), which arguably fits better there. The line-splitting theme is nearly identical. The comments theme matches but includes an invented issue, #3651, which the report itself marks as "(not in the repo)". That is a fabricated entry. The configuration theme matches, except that #3769 (--diff line numbers) is misplaced there and #5546 (cache pickle) is moved to the performance/security theme, which is defensible. #4438 (free-threaded build) is moved to performance, which is plausible. Integrations is merged into release/packaging, collapsing two labelled themes. These are mostly minor misplacements plus a hallucinated issue, so this is mostly the labelled groupings with a few errors.

themes.name: Preview/unstable style features and the 2027 stable style
Configuration, file discovery and target-version inference

top_issues.reason: Security hardening: a relative cache-dir set in the project config leads to pickle.load of files the repository author controls, which can run arbitrary code when Black runs with caching on.
Black silently skips files that git tracks when a nested .gitignore uses a negation, so `black --check` can pass in CI without a warning. A small fix is proposed.
Tracking issue for deciding the 2027 stable style. It sets the direction for many open preview-style issues.
requires-python `~=3.11.0` infers target versions the project does not support. Several PRs are already open.
Black hangs forever on deeply nested long dicts, a performance bug that can block users and CI.

records.judge_reason: The report's themes closely match the labelled ones. Comments/pragmas is identical. Line-splitting/style is nearly identical, minus #5658, which the report moved into the preview/string-processing theme. That theme otherwise matches the labelled string processing and preview theme exactly, and placing #5658 there is defensible. Configuration matches, with two differences: #5546 (cache pickle security) moved to a performance/security theme, which is reasonable, and #3769 (--diff line numbers) was added, which is a slight misplacement. The performance theme gains #5546 and #4438 (free-threaded build), and the latter fits only marginally. Releases and integrations were merged into one theme. The merge is coherent but less granular. Overall these are mostly the labelled groupings with a few misplacements and one merge.

themes.name: Configuration, file discovery and target-version inference

top_issues.reason: Security hardening: a relative cache-dir set in project config lets crafted pickle files in an untrusted checkout run arbitrary code when Black is run on it.
Black silently skips files that git tracks when a nested .gitignore uses a negation, so --check passes without checking them; seen in major repos and a small fix has been proposed.
Inferring target versions from a ~= requires-python constraint picks Python versions the project does not support; there is a clear repro and PRs are already open.
Planning issue for which preview features become the 2027 stable style; time-sensitive, and many preview-feedback issues depend on it.
Black hangs with no message on a pathological file, which stalls CI and tooling without any explanation.

records.judge_reason: The report closely follows the labelled groupings, with a few deviations. Matching themes: configuration and file discovery, line splitting and style, comments and pragmas, and string processing and preview features. The report merged two labelled themes, performance/hangs and releases/packaging, into one. It then also dissolved the integrations/output theme: three of its issues (#4156, #3571, #4025) went into that merged performance/packaging bucket, where they fit poorly, and #3769 (diff output) went into configuration. Smaller misplacements: #5658 (2027 stable style) moved to preview, which is arguable. #3714 (comments in parentheses) and #3518 (fmt wrap-list directive) moved to line breaking. Most groupings are intact, but one theme is a mixed catch-all and a few issues are misplaced.

themes.name: Resolver failures and dependency resolution behaviour
CLI error handling, output header and writer UX
Project maintenance, CI, security policy and docs

top_issues.reason: Regression in 7.6.1+: --generate-hashes skips the PyPI JSON API and downloads every file (GBs of data). Dependabot is affected, a one-line fix is known and a maintainer confirmed it.
Labelled regression: since 6.10.0, pip-compile hangs when its input is a named pipe because the input is read twice.
No security reporting policy since leaving Jazzband. Private reporting is now enabled and a SECURITY policy still needs to be written.
Invalid --max-rounds values crash with a traceback. An easy fix (#2510) is open, but one test needs reworking first.
pip-sync breaks its own install on Windows when the lock file pins a different pip-tools version, and the README describes this behaviour wrongly.

records.judge_reason: The maintenance/CI, pip-sync, resolver and hashes/caching themes largely match the labelled groupings. Several placements are wrong, though. #1836, #1831 and #2160 sit in the maintenance theme even though they are not maintenance issues. #2080 (PEP 740) is in hashes. #2096 and #2125 (config) are in pip-sync. The report has no separate config theme; config issues are scattered across 'packaging standards and new features', which is a vague catch-all mixing PEP work with feature requests on output, annotations, credentials and private URLs. The CLI/output theme is reasonably coherent but merges error handling with header issues. Overall some themes match well, but one theme is a grab-bag and there is a fair number of misplacements.

duplicates.reason: Same root cause: the eager --config callback runs before src_files is parsed, so config discovery uses the wrong directory. A maintainer comment on 2096 points to 1902, and 2096 is already labelled duplicate.

Both report ResolutionImpossible because pip-compile keeps a stale transitive pin from the existing requirements.txt instead of dropping it when requirements.in changes. Deleting the pin, or using --upgrade, works around it in both.

The project needs a security reporting policy after leaving Jazzband. Private reporting is already enabled, but the policy text is still missing.

records.judge_reason: The maintenance/CI, pip-sync, hashes/caching and resolver themes largely match the labels. duplicates.reason: Both report that reduplicated kinship words such as 爸爸 get full tones instead of a neutral tone on the second syllable.

Both ask for surname-specific polyphone handling for personal names, e.g. 查 read as zhā; the maintainer linked 297 to 120.

top_issues.reason: heteronym=True returns readings most users don't expect for very common characters (受→dào, 惊→liáng, etc.); still open as of 0.55.0. The maintainer says many come from rare dictionary readings, so this needs a decision on whether to filter them by default.
Neutral tone is never applied to very common words. Three issues (246, 316, 359) report it, and it hurts output for learners.
General inaccuracy in picking the right reading for polyphonic characters, the library's core feature; it has an active discussion.
Surnames with several readings are converted wrongly; a long-asked-for feature (see 120) that already comes with a ready-made list of surname readings.
A common phrase (目标识别) gets the wrong reading because of segmentation. The maintainer says the latest release adjusts the reading of 标识; check that this fixes it and close.

records.judge_reason: The report closely mirrors the labelled structure. The wrong-readings theme matches almost exactly; #263 moves to the polyphone theme, and #284 and #249 come in, both of which are defensible. This is a reasonable regrouping, not a mix of unrelated topics. The APIs/output theme matches the labelled styles theme, with #362, #307 and #184 moved in from elsewhere, which is defensible since they are feature requests. The ports/data theme matches, though #133 (accuracy evaluation) fits less well there. Overall the groupings are coherent, with some theme boundaries shifted and a few issues placed debatably. The heteronym and tone split differs from the labels but is not worse.
